lead.headline: September 15 estimated-tax deadline approaches for many self-employed taxpayers
lead.summary: The IRS lists September 15 as the third 2026 estimated-tax payment deadline for calendar-year individuals.
lead.why_it_matters: Freelancers, gig workers, sole proprietors and others whose income is not fully covered by withholding may need to review their federal estimated-tax obligation before Tuesday.
body: The third federal estimated-tax payment for 2026 is due Tuesday, September 15, for calendar-year individuals who are required to make quarterly payments, according to the Internal Revenue Service’s current Form 1040-ES instructions.

Estimated tax commonly applies when income is not fully covered by withholding. The IRS lists self-employment and gig-economy earnings, interest, dividends, rent and certain other taxable income among the situations that can create an estimated-tax obligation.

Individuals, including sole proprietors, partners and S corporation shareholders, generally may need estimated payments when they expect to owe at least $1,000 after subtracting withholding and refundable credits. The calculation also depends on how current-year withholding compares with current- and prior-year tax, and special rules can apply to higher-income taxpayers, farmers and fishers.

The IRS says taxpayers can use the 2026 Form 1040-ES worksheet to recalculate payments when income or circumstances change. Payment options include an IRS online account, Direct Pay, EFTPS, phone, mobile device or mail; mailed payments are subject to federal postmark rules.

This is general deadline information, not individualized tax advice. Hawaiʻi residents should review the official IRS form and payment guidance or consult a qualified tax professional about their own filing status, income, withholding, disaster-related circumstances and any separate Hawaiʻi estimated-tax requirements.

stories.headline: Lifeline Awareness Week highlights help with phone and internet costs
stories.summary: The Hawaiʻi Public Utilities Commission is directing qualifying households to the federal Lifeline program during September 13–19.
stories.why_it_matters: Reliable phone and internet access can connect residents with emergency services, health care, work, school and family resources.
body: Hawaiʻi’s Public Utilities Commission is using National Digital Connectivity and Lifeline Awareness Week, September 13–19, to remind residents about a federal program that can reduce qualifying phone and internet costs.

The Federal Communications Commission’s Lifeline program offers eligible households a monthly discount of up to $9.25 for qualifying internet or bundled phone-and-internet service, or up to $5.25 for voice-only phone service, according to the PUC.
Eligibility generally depends on household income or participation in certain federal assistance programs. The PUC does not process applications or decide whether an individual qualifies.

Residents can review complete eligibility requirements, apply and locate participating providers through LifelineSupport.org. The Lifeline Support Center is also available at 1-800-234-9473 for questions about eligibility, applications or an existing benefit.

The program is intended to make essential communications more affordable for qualifying households. Applicants should rely on the official Lifeline site for current requirements and should not send personal eligibility information to PinoyLink.
